title: ～て済む — “get by with ～ / manage with just ～”
summary: 済む means “to be finished, to be settled.” Used after a noun with で, or a negative te-form (～なくて済む), it says that a problem was solved with a small effort or without the unpleasant action. The tone is relieved.

patterns.form: 名詞 ＋ で ＋ 済む／済ませる
patterns.gloss: noun + で + 済む (電話一本で済みました), 済ませる (パン一個で済ませた)

patterns.form: 動詞ない形 ＋ なくて／ないで ＋ 済む
patterns.gloss: ~なくて／ないで + 済む = didn't have to ～ (歩かなくて済んだ)

body.p: The noun is a small amount or simple means, and で means “by, with.” 電話一本で済みました (it was settled with one call). The transitive 済ませる is used when the speaker does it on purpose: パン一個で済ませた (I made do with one bread roll).
～なくて済む / ～ないで済む means “I didn't have to do ～.” 歩かなくて済んだ means that, luckily, walking was not necessary. It often shows relief at escaping something troublesome.
Do not use it to describe a bare end of an action. For “finish,” use 終わる or ～てしまう. 済む emphasizes that the matter ended with little cost.

examples.ja: その件（けん）は電話（でんわ）一本（いっぽん）で済（す）みました。
examples.romaji: Sono ken wa denwa ippon de sumimashita.
examples.tr: That matter was settled with just one phone call.

examples.ja: 昼食（ちゅうしょく）は、パン一個（いっこ）で済（す）ませた。
examples.romaji: Chūshoku wa, pan ikko de sumaseta.
examples.tr: I got by with just one bread roll for lunch.

examples.ja: 電車（でんしゃ）が動（うご）いていたので、歩（ある）かなくて済（す）んだ。
examples.romaji: Densha ga ugoite ita node, arukanakute sunda.
examples.tr: The trains were running, so I didn't have to walk.

pitfalls: Do not use it for an ordinary ending. 仕事が済んだ is fine, but the pattern here means being settled with little cost.
With the negative, the form is ～なくて済む (or ～ないで済む), not ～ないて済む.
